messages:
alex: Heads up — EU fleet (n1@eu-west) is in sustained saturation window, queues are growing and clients are seeing a bunch of 429s. Retry-After values are all over the place. Anyone watching admission controller metrics?

maria: Yep, seeing the same. Admission controller emitting high admission scores; SDKs treat the 429 as terminal and start retry storms. Also noticing clients don't look at our admission headers today.

samir: Can we emit a more explicit client-facing hint? Something like an advisory header with suggested backoff/jitter and a preferred fallback region? Right now clients only see Retry-After/429 and do dumb exponential retries.

leo: We already have internal admission metrics but not a single easy header. Proposals: either (A) augment 429 with a structured header (compact key=val list) including capacity_pct + suggested_delay + prefer_region, or (B) return 202 for long queueable workloads. Both have tradeoffs.

maria: I would avoid 202 for interactive endpoints (chat/generate) — polling is awkward. 202 could work for embeddings/batch. For RL-type workloads we should keep 429 but make it advisory, e.g. both Retry-After and a new X-Redwood-Admission header containing: status=soft|hard;retry_after=secs;capacity_pct=NN;pref_region=xxx

alex: Also need clear client guidance: when Admission status=soft => clients should reduce concurrency (halve inflight requests), apply full jitter backoff with max_backoff=10s, and avoid aggressive immediate retries. If capacity_pct < 50 => step down concurrency; if < 20 => fall back to lower-cost queued path.

ingrid: Infra can spin an emergency autoscale in eu-west for ~20m and divert non-critical traffic to dedicated pool, but cost will spike. If SDKs can gracefully reduce concurrency we might avoid the autoscale.

samir: Alternative idea — admission controller can reply with 202+queue_pos+eta for batch paths. That prevents client retries entirely: clients poll or accept a webhook. Worth trying for embeddings.

leo: Agreed on structured header. To minimise churn, let's standardise on a single header: X-Redwood-Admission. Example payload:

```
X-Redwood-Admission: status=soft;retry_after=3;capacity_pct=42;pref_region=us-west;queue_pos=12
```

maria: That looks fine. We'll also keep Retry-After on hard 429s. For soft status clients should do local queuing: hold request in client queue (bounded) and retry after suggested delay with jitter rather than reattempt instantly.

alex: Quick SDK spec suggestion (for eng-runtime + client libs):
- honor X-Redwood-Admission=status=soft => don't increment global error counter, apply local backoff and reduce concurrency by 50%
- use capacity_pct to scale concurrency: new_limit = max(1, floor(current_limit * capacity_pct/100))
- on status=hard => observe Retry-After and apply capped exponential backoff with full jitter (cap 10s)
- if pref_region present and latency delta < 200ms => attempt failover to pref_region endpoint once

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: admission-controller v2 rolled out to eu-west at 09:18 UTC (50% of nodes). New header X-Redwood-Admission emitted by default.

leo: I'll draft a short RFC with header grammar + SDK change list. Maria, can you add a short migration note for client teams and embed a tiny snippet on how to parse header?

maria: On it. I'll also add a compatibility footer: if clients don't understand header, server keeps sending 429s as before for hard overloads but will set soft status for a grace period so we can observe client behavior.

samir: One more ask — include minimal rate token info when applicable, e.g.: rate=50/s;burst=200 so smart SDKs can shape the request rate instead of hammering. Put that in the same header to avoid header explosion.

alex: Thanks all. Priorities: (1) RFC + SDK updates, (2) monitor for client adoption over next 2 hours, (3) infra standby for autoscale if adoption lagging.

leo: pinging client teams in #devex to fast-track SDK patch.

maria: Filing the RFC now: https://redwood/internal/rfcs/adm-header-2026 — will include examples and exact field list.

alex: :thumbsup:
